Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star two. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; and Taylor Kim, Chief Revenue Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on four key areas: advancing our product roadmap, strengthening our LTV/CAC ratio, growing our average contract value, and accelerating ARR growth both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter.

Let me start with our product roadmap. As we wrap up a strong quarter with ARR growth of 28% year-over-year to $450 million and net revenue retention holding steady at 118%, I want to spend a few minutes updating you on our product initiatives. Our engineering and product teams have been laser-focused on delivering high-impact innovations that drive customer value, sticky usage, and expansion within our land-and-expand model. We've seen firsthand how these investments are accelerating our Rule of 40 score to 62%, blending 28% growth with 34% FCF margins.

In Q3, we shipped 14 major features across our core CloudForge CRM platform and our CloudForge Analytics suite—up 40% from last year—reaching over 12,000 customers. Adoption metrics are exceeding our internal targets: 65% of our enterprise cohort activated at least three new features within 30 days, contributing to a 15% uplift in quarterly active users, or QAU, now at 87% of our paid seat base. This is fueling our dollar-based net expansion rate, as upsell from feature unlocks represented 22% of total bookings this quarter.

Diving into key initiatives, our flagship AI push with CloudForge Intelligence continues to be a game-changer. Building on the momentum from our Einstein-like predictive engine launched last year—which now powers 72% of sales forecasts across our top 500 accounts—we rolled out Intelligent Deal Scoring 2.0 in early September. This leverages our proprietary fine-tuned LLM, trained on 15 billion anonymized interaction tokens from our multi-tenant data lake, to deliver probabilistic win-rate predictions with 92% accuracy, up from 84% in v1. Early results show deal velocity increased 18% for users, and we've seen a 25% reduction in sales cycle times for mid-market segments. Over 4,500 teams have adopted it, with NRR from AI users at 125%—significantly outpacing our platform average.

Complementing this, we're addressing the collaboration explosion post-pandemic with CloudForge Workspaces, our Slack/Teams-native overlay launched last month. This isn't just another integration; it's a full-context sync with real-time co-editing of deal pipelines, powered by WebSocket APIs and our new GraphQL federation layer for sub-100ms latency. We've integrated with 18 third-party apps out of the gate, including Zoom, Gong, and Outreach, and regional feedback has been stellar: in EMEA, where remote selling is 40% higher than NA due to GDPR-driven hybrid models, adoption hit 52% among our 2,100 customers there, driving 30% MoM growth in collaborative session minutes.

On the technical front, scalability remains core to our multi-tenant architecture. We migrated 80% of our workloads to Kubernetes on AWS Graviton3 instances in Q3, slashing compute costs by 28% while boosting throughput 3x during peak surges. This underpins CloudForge Edge, our new serverless compute layer for custom workflows—think Zapier on steroids with native zero-trust security via mTLS and SODA-compliant data residency. Beta testers in APAC, where we've doubled our seat growth to 1.2 million amid Singapore's Smart Nation push, report 45% faster workflow execution, positioning us against regional players like Kingdee.

Vertically, we're tailoring for high-growth sectors. Our Healthcare Module—HIPAA and HITRUST certified—launched with FHIR API interoperability, capturing 18% of our bookings from providers like regional hospital networks. In financial services, CloudForge Compliance Hub now embeds SOC 2 Type II controls with automated audit trails, resonating in a post-FTX world where 35% of fintechs cite regtech as their top priority per Gartner.

Regionally, we're accelerating localization. APAC now represents 22% of ARR, up from 15% YoY, fueled by Japanese and Korean language packs and J-SOX alignment. In LATAM, our Spanish/Portuguese expansions have driven 55% YoY customer growth, though macro headwinds like Brazil's inflation are tempering seat expansion—we're countering with flexible per-user pricing tiers that boosted conversion by 12%.

Looking ahead to H2, we're teeing up CloudForge Autonomous Agents, GA in Q4, which will handle end-to-end lead nurturing using agentic AI workflows—think multi-step reasoning chains rivaling Adept or Salesforce's Agentforce. Early pilots with 200 beta customers show 40% productivity gains for SDRs. We'll also launch No-Code Studio, empowering rev ops teams to build custom apps 5x faster than OutSystems, with projected 30% adoption in SMBs by year-end.

Strategically, these initiatives align with three pillars: AI ubiquity to combat commoditization, ecosystem density to raise switching costs (our 250+ integrations now average 4.2 per customer), and vertical depth to premiumize pricing—enterprise ACV up 22% to $185k. Amidst market softness, like the 8% SaaS multiple contraction YTD per Bessemer, our roadmap is derisking growth through proven monetization: new features contribute 16% to expansion revenue.

We're excited about the flywheel effect—customer feedback loops via our Canny-powered ideation portal have a 75% implementation rate—and we'll share more at Dreamforce in September.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders, with improving LTV/CAC, rising ACV, and robust ARR growth underpinning our path forward.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $115 million, representing a 35% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $22 million.

Turning to ARR growth, which continues to be the bedrock of our SaaS flywheel here at CloudForge. Annual Recurring Revenue—or ARR—is our north star metric, capturing the annualized value of our subscription contracts net of churn, contractions, and expansions. We're thrilled to report that total ARR reached $452 million at the end of Q3 FY2024, up 41% year-over-year from $320 million in Q3 FY2023, and 8% quarter-over-quarter from $418 million at the end of Q2.

This 41% YoY growth marks our 12th straight quarter of 40%+ expansion, outpacing the SaaS industry average of around 25-30% as reported in recent Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud indices. It's fueled by a healthy mix of drivers. New logo ACV came in at $185K, up 15% YoY, driven by our enterprise wins in the Fortune 1000. We landed 28 deals over $1M in total contract value, including a landmark expansion with a major fintech player akin to Stripe, who adopted our full AI-Augmented Pipeline Suite across their entire DevOps stack.

On the QoQ front, that 8% sequential growth reflects the power of our land-and-expand model. Net Revenue Retention—or NRR—held steady at 118%, meaning our existing customers are expanding with us at a robust clip. Expansions accounted for 42% of this quarter's dollar-based net expansion rate, with upsells into our premium tiers like ForgeAI Optimizer and Multi-Cloud Orchestrator. For context, this NRR is in line with category leaders like Snowflake or Datadog, but we're gaining share in the $50B+ DevOps platform market, where Gartner pegs our fast follower status behind incumbents like GitLab and Atlassian.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, contributing 62% of ARR with 45% YoY growth, propelled by hyperscaler partnerships—think deepened integrations with AWS Bedrock and Azure DevOps—that reduced deployment TTV from weeks to hours. EMEA surged 55% YoY to 22% of total ARR, thanks to GDPR-compliant features and wins in banking verticals like those serving Deutsche Bank-scale clients. APAC, now 12% of ARR, grew 65% YoY on the back of our Tokyo data center launch and localization efforts, though we saw some forex headwinds from a stronger USD. LatAm is nascent at 4%, but up 80% with early traction in Brazil's fintech boom.

Strategically, this ARR acceleration ties directly to our technical initiatives. Q3 saw the GA of ForgeAI 2.0, our generative AI copilot that automates 70% of CI/CD pipeline debugging—early adopters are seeing 40% faster release cycles, directly correlating to higher seat expansions. We've also doubled down on security with Zero-Trust Pipeline Enforcement, resonating amid rising supply chain attacks like those highlighted in the Log4j saga. Churn remains elite at 3.8% gross dollar-based, below the 5-7% SaaS benchmark from KeyBanc, underscoring sticky product-market fit.

Looking ahead, we see Q4 YoY ARR growth in the mid-30% range, conservatively guiding to $485M+ by year-end, as macro tailwinds like AI infra spend—projected at $200B globally per McKinsey—play to our strengths. We're not chasing growth at all costs; our Rule of 60 score hit 68 this quarter (50% YoY growth + 18% FCF margin), balancing efficiency with expansion.

Next, I'd like to highlight our Average Contract Value, or ACV, which came in at $52,300 for the quarter—up 22% year-over-year from $42,800 in Q3 FY23, and a solid 8% sequentially from $48,400 in Q2 FY24. This marks our sixth straight quarter of double-digit YoY ACV growth, underscoring the premium value our platform delivers in a market where customers are prioritizing AI-driven outcomes amid macroeconomic headwinds.

To give you a fuller picture, new business ACV—our wins with net new logos—reached $61,500, a robust 28% YoY increase from $48,000 last year. This acceleration reflects our strategic pivot toward enterprise-scale deployments, where we're landing multi-year contracts bundled with our new ForgeAI suite. Deals over $100K ACV now represent 35% of new bookings, up from just 18% a year ago—think transformative wins like our recent expansions with Fortune 500 names in financial services, similar to how Snowflake has scaled its AI Data Cloud ACVs through hyperscaler integrations.

On the expansion side, renewal and upsell ACV held steady at $47,200, up 12% YoY, driven by net revenue retention of 118%—our strongest in two years. Customers are expanding seats and modules at a 15% attach rate for ForgeAI, which adds predictive analytics and workflow automation on top of our core collaboration tools. This mirrors trends we've seen at peers like ServiceNow, where AI upsells have boosted expansion ACV by 20-25% in recent quarters.

Segment-wise, enterprise ACV—deals over 500 seats—jumped 32% YoY to $89,400, fueled by six-figure logos in healthcare and manufacturing, where regulatory compliance features command premiums. Mid-market ACV grew 19% to $38,700, benefiting from our simplified self-serve onboarding, while SMB ACV ticked up modestly 5% to $12,500. We're not chasing volume at the low end; instead, we're guiding SMBs toward mid-market tiers via usage-based pricing pilots, which have converted 22% of pilots to expansions in Q3.

Regionally, North America remains our ACV powerhouse at $58,200—up 25% YoY—accounting for 72% of total ACV as enterprises accelerate digital transformation post the generative AI hype cycle. EMEA saw a standout 41% YoY surge to $42,100, propelled by GDPR-aligned AI governance tools and wins with DAX-listed firms, outpacing the region's 12% SaaS market growth per Gartner. APAC lagged slightly at 14% YoY growth to $39,800, but we're optimistic with recent hyperscaler partnerships—like our AWS Marketplace co-sell with Amazon Bedrock integrations—that should unlock Japan and ANZ enterprise deals in H2.

Strategically, these trends stem from three key initiatives. First, our ForgeAI launch in Q4 FY23, now embedded in 65% of new contracts, lifts ACV by an average 32% through modular pricing—customers pay $15K-$25K annually for advanced features like real-time anomaly detection, akin to Databricks' MosaicML uplift. Second, we've shifted to outcome-based contracts, with 40% of Q3 deals tying ACV to ROI milestones, reducing churn risk and aligning with CIO budgets squeezed by inflation. Third, land-and-expand efficiency: our median time to $100K ACV customer is down to 14 months from 20, thanks to API extensibility with Salesforce Einstein and Microsoft Copilot ecosystems.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 ACV to land in the $54,000-$56,000 range, with 20%+ YoY growth, as we roll out ForgeAI Pro for verticals like retail and CPG. Risks include forex volatility in EMEA and SMB caution amid high interest rates, but our 85% gross retention and focus on high-ACV verticals position us resiliently. This ACV momentum, paired with our 125% dollar-based net expansion rate, gives us high conviction in our $1.2B FY24 revenue guide.

Now, turning to one of our core efficiency metrics: our Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost, or LTV/CAC ratio. For those new to our story, this ratio is a North Star for SaaS businesses like CloudForge, measuring the long-term economic value we capture from each customer relative to the upfront investment required to acquire them. It's calculated as LTV—our projected net profit over a customer's lifetime—divided by CAC, the fully loaded cost of sales and marketing to land that customer. A healthy ratio above 3x signals sustainable unit economics, allowing us to scale profitably even in a high-interest-rate environment where capital efficiency is paramount.

I'm pleased to report that in Q3, our LTV/CAC ratio strengthened to 4.2x, up from 3.8x in Q2 and a robust improvement from 3.4x a year ago. This puts us in the upper echelon of the SaaS peer set—think companies like Snowflake or HubSpot, which have historically traded around 4-5x during expansion phases. For context, our LTV stands at $48,000 on a cohort basis, driven by an average ARPU of $1,200 annually across our mid-market and enterprise segments, multiplied by our 85%+ gross margins and an estimated customer lifetime of 42 months (derived from 2.3% monthly churn, or 28% ARR churn). Meanwhile, CAC has held steady at $11,400, reflecting disciplined spend on a blended basis: $8,500 for enterprise deals via field sales and $4,200 for SMB self-serve.

Let me break down the key drivers of this 10% QoQ uplift. First, product-led growth initiatives are accelerating payback periods. We've doubled down on our AI-powered freemium tier, inspired by successes at Notion and Linear, where viral loops and in-app upsells convert 18% of free users to paid within 90 days—up from 12% last year. This has slashed SMB CAC by 22% YoY, as organic channels now account for 35% of net new ARR, reducing our reliance on paid ads. Technically, our new ForgeAI Predict feature uses machine learning models trained on 5+ years of usage data to personalize onboarding nudges, boosting activation rates by 15% and extending Day 90 retention to 92%.

Second, enterprise upsell velocity is firing on all cylinders. Our focus on land-and-expand with modules like Advanced Workflow Automation and Compliance Guardrails—akin to ServiceNow's Now Platform strategy—has pushed expansion revenue to 28% of total ARR, the highest in our history. For logos over $100K ACV, LTV has ballooned to $185,000, with multi-year contracts now at 65% mix. This cohort's LTV/CAC is an enviable 6.1x, offsetting softer SMB dynamics.

Regionally, the story is bifurcated but trending positively. North America remains our fortress, contributing 72% of ARR with a stellar 4.6x ratio, fueled by hyperscaler partnerships like AWS Marketplace integrations that cut CAC by 30% via co-marketing credits. EMEA has caught fire at 3.9x—up from 3.1x LY—thanks to GDPR-compliant AI features and a dedicated localization team targeting DACH markets; we're now at 15% regional ARR share. APAC lags at 2.9x due to longer sales cycles and competition from local players like Kingdee, but our Q3 pilot with Tencent Cloud has unlocked 50+ beta customers, and we expect breakeven economics by Q1 '25 as we refine channel partnerships.

Looking at trends, our Rule of 40 score—blending 32% YoY ARR growth and 18% FCF margin—is now 50, firmly in elite territory. We've modeled forward: at current trajectories, LTV/CAC should hit 4.5x by year-end, assuming churn holds below 2.5% monthly. Risks? Macro headwinds could pressure SMB renewals, but our 120%+ Net Retention Rate provides a buffer, outperforming median SaaS benchmarks from Bessemer Venture Partners' State of the Cloud report.

Strategically, we're not resting on this. Q4 priorities include AI-optimized CAC allocation: using predictive analytics to shift 20% more budget from broad Google Ads to high-intent LinkedIn targeting, aiming for 15% CAC reduction; cohort-based pricing experiments: testing usage-based models like those at Snowflake to boost ARPU by 10-15% without churn spikes; and global expansion playbook: $50M investment in EMEA/APAC ABM to mirror our NA playbook, targeting 4x ratios enterprise-wide by FY '26.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $350 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first three quarters of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $475 million to $485 million.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with Morgan Stanley.

Ben Thompson:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been transformative, as I touched on earlier. With features like Intelligent Deal Scoring 2.0 achieving 92% accuracy in win-rate predictions and adoption by over 4,500 teams, it's driving 18% higher deal velocity and 25% shorter sales cycles. AI users are showing 125% NRR, contributing 22% to total bookings via upsells, and it's a key factor in our 41% YoY ARR growth and 118% NRR. We're seeing it embedded in 65% of new contracts, lifting ACV by 32% on average.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with JPMorgan.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks for the question, Lisa. Internationally, we're making strong progress. APAC now at 22% of ARR, up from 15% YoY, with Tokyo data center, language packs, and pilots like Tencent Cloud pushing 65% growth and unlocking 50+ betas. EMEA at 22% of ARR with 55% YoY surge via GDPR tools and DACH focus, hitting 41% ACV growth. LATAM up 55% customers with flexible pricing countering inflation. H2 priorities include $50M in ABM, hyperscaler co-sells like AWS Bedrock, and localization to drive 4x LTV/CAC enterprise-wide by FY26, targeting mid-30% YoY ARR in Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Barclays.

Mike Patel:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Mike. Our gross dollar-based churn is elite at 3.8%, below 5-7% benchmarks, with 85% gross retention. Monthly churn at 2.3% supports 42-month lifetimes. Buffers include 118-125% NRR, 92% Day 90 retention from PLG nudges, and sticky AI features like ForgeAI automating workflows for 40% productivity gains. Risks like SMB macro are offset by enterprise expansions at 28% of ARR, multi-year contracts at 65% mix, and vertical premiums. We're prioritizing usage-based pricing and ROI-tied deals to hold churn under 2.5% monthly.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Product roadmap: Provide updates on key product initiatives and feature launches.
LTV/CAC ratio: Report the Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio.
Average contract value (ACV): Report and explain trends in average contract value.
ARR growth (YoY and QoQ): Report actual ARR and percentage growth.

aspect_summary.Product roadmap: Shipped 14 major features (up 40% YoY) across CRM and Analytics; key launches include Intelligent Deal Scoring 2.0 (92% accuracy, 18% deal velocity increase), CloudForge Workspaces (high EMEA adoption), CloudForge Edge, Healthcare Module, Compliance Hub; upcoming Q4: Autonomous Agents, No-Code Studio.
aspect_summary.LTV/CAC ratio: Q3 LTV/CAC at 4.2x (up from 3.8x QoQ, 3.4x YoY); LTV $48k, CAC $11.4k; driven by PLG/AI freemium (SMB CAC -22% YoY), enterprise upsells; regional: NA 4.6x, EMEA 3.9x, APAC 2.9x; expect 4.5x year-end.
aspect_summary.Average contract value (ACV): Q3 ACV $52.3k (+22% YoY from $42.8k, +8% QoQ from $48.4k); new business $61.5k (+28% YoY), enterprise $89.4k (+32% YoY); trends from AI bundles, enterprise focus, regional strength (NA +25%, EMEA +41%); Q4 guide $54-56k (+20%+ YoY).
aspect_summary.ARR growth (YoY and QoQ): Q3 ARR $452M (+41% YoY from $320M, +8% QoQ from $418M); 12th straight 40%+ YoY quarter; driven by new logos ($185k ACV), expansions (NRR 118%), regional growth (NA 45%, EMEA 55%, APAC 65%); Q4 guide mid-30% YoY to $485M+.
